supporting_observations.claim: WS-KNGUYEN-01 made a series of similarly sized connections to 10.52.20.30:8080 at approximately five-minute intervals: 13:45:57, 13:51:18, 13:56:43, 14:01:30, and 14:06:14 UTC. The records show roughly 7.5 KB sent and 20 KB received per connection.

The observed cadence is consistent with the inventory description of the approved RouteWise updater checking for updates about every five minutes, but the available records do not establish that RouteWise generated these connections.
The connection records identify the proxy endpoint and traffic volumes, but do not show the requested destination, URL, or originating process.

known_telemetry_limitations: The available network records show connections to 10.52.20.30:8080 but do not include proxy request or CONNECT details identifying the external destination.
The records do not identify which process on WS-KNGUYEN-01 initiated the periodic connections.
The provided records do not independently confirm that the connections used HTTPS or that their destination was update.routewise.com.
claims_not_established: That the periodic connections were generated by the approved RouteWise updater.
That the connections reached update.routewise.com or another approved destination.
That the alerted activity was malicious or benign.
additional_evidence_needed: Proxy logs for the listed timestamps, including CONNECT target or hostname, URL where available, and response details.
Endpoint process or EDR telemetry for WS-KNGUYEN-01 at the listed timestamps to identify the process responsible.
DNS or TLS SNI records that could associate the connections with a destination domain.
unrelated_findings: At 13:22:12 UTC, WS-KNGUYEN-01 made an SSH connection to 10.52.20.30:22. The inventory says remote administration is only done from WS-PBECKER-01; investigate separately. This observation does not determine the disposition of the alerted periodic connections. (T116-00022)
